in_distribution_retrieval_comparison.scientific_interpretation: The 2 percentage point difference (10% vs 12%) is based on only 8 discordant pairs out of 100 items (Treatment succeeded where Control failed on 5 items; Control succeeded where Treatment failed on 3 items). McNemar's test yields chi2=0.125, p=0.7237, demonstrating NO statistically significant difference (p >> 0.05). The 95% confidence intervals heavily overlap ([5.52%, 17.44%] vs [6.97%, 19.89%]). Therefore, the hypothesis that a 5.0x loss multiplier yields superior retrieval over standard SFT is UNFOUNDED.

conversational_preservation_small_sample.scientific_interpretation: The reported difference in conversational preservation (58.33% vs 41.67%) corresponds to an absolute difference of EXACTLY TWO PROBES (7/12 vs 5/12 hits) on an extremely small sample of n=12 probes. The 95% Wilson confidence intervals ([31.95%, 80.67%] vs [19.33%, 68.05%]) heavily overlap by nearly 36 percentage points. While Treatment Arm B trended lower in fluency, claiming that 5.0x loss weighting conclusively 'damaged' conversational capability overinterprets an effect spanning just two test items.
